collection.description: A villager is the smallest child in the village and the most afraid of everything: the dark, the sea, the pigs, the drums.

ask.text:
(subject) is the smallest child in the village and the most afraid of everything: the dark, the sea, the pigs, the drums. The other children tease (subject.him/her) about it. Today (subject) has decided to be brave, all at once, and has announced (subject.he/she) is going to spend a whole night alone in the old hut on the hill, which everyone knows is haunted.
(elder) has heard about it, and comes to find (subject) packing a basket. (subject.He/She) says the old hut belonged to (subject.his/her) own grandmother, who was "a little bit magic," and that brave children who sleep there sometimes wake up older than they went to bed. "Not always," (subject.he/she) says. "But sometimes."
Should (subject) go to the hut, or stay home?

c1o1.text: In the morning (subject) walks down the hill, and the other children don't recognise (subject.him/her). (subject.He/She) is fifteen: tall, long-legged, and not afraid of anything, or at least not afraid of the things (subject.he/she) was afraid of yesterday. (elder) is not at all surprised. "Grandmother liked brave ones," (elder.he/she) says. The teasing stops at once.

c1o2.text: Nothing happens all night except creaks and an owl. In the morning (subject) walks down the hill exactly the same age, and much braver. Two things (subject.he/she) has always hated, (subject.he/she) suddenly doesn't. The other children want to hear all about the haunted hut. (subject) tells them the owl was a ghost, because it's a better story.

c1.text: (subject) climbs the hill at sunset with a basket and a blanket and a very small torch. The hut is dark and smells of old herbs. (subject.He/She) lies down, eyes wide open, and listens to every creak...

c2o1.text: (elder) tells (subject) the whole story of (subject.his/her) grandmother, who was afraid of everything as a child too, and grew up to be the bravest person on the island. (subject) listens till (subject.he/she) falls asleep on the doorstep. The next day, (subject.he/she) walks past the pigs without running. It's a start.

c2o2.text: (subject) stays home that night. But the next night, without telling anyone, (subject.he/she) goes up to the hut after all, alone, and sleeps there till dawn. When (subject.he/she) comes down, (subject.he/she) is fourteen. (elder) sees (subject.him/her) on the path and laughs out loud. "Grandmother liked brave ones," (elder.he/she) says. "Especially stubborn ones."

c2.text: (subject) looks at the hill, and the dark coming down, and unpacks the basket. (elder) sits down beside (subject.him/her) on the doorstep. "Brave isn't only doing the scary thing," (elder.he/she) says. "Want to hear about Grandmother?"
